question: A physician attempts to study cirrhosis in his state. Using a registry of admitted patients over the last 10 years at the local hospital, he isolates all patients who have been diagnosed with cirrhosis. Subsequently, he contacts this group of patients, asking them to complete a survey assessing their prior exposure to alcohol use, intravenous drug abuse, blood transfusions, personal history of cancer, and other medical comorbidities. An identical survey is given to an equal number of patients in the registry who do not carry a prior diagnosis of cirrhosis. Which of the following is the study design utilized by this physician?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Exposure assessment -> Comparison of groups with and without cirrhosis -> Case-control study design -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Survey completion on cirrhosis patients and non-cirrhosis patients -> Data collection on alcohol use, drug abuse, transfusions, cancer history -> Case-control study design -> 95%
analysis: The study design utilized by the physician in this scenario is a case-control study. This is evident as the physician has identified individuals with cirrhosis (cases) and compared them to individuals without cirrhosis (controls) to assess the association between various exposures and the development of cirrhosis.
